No, an HIV1/2 point of care test on sputum will not work for screening TB/HIV co-infection. 

HIV point of care tests typically require a blood or oral fluid sample to detect the presence of HIV antibodies, not sputum. Sputum is used to diagnose tuberculosis (TB), not HIV. 

To screen for TB/HIV co-infection, you would need to use two separate tests: 

1. A sputum test (such as smear microscopy, GeneXpert, or culture) to diagnose TB.
2. A blood or oral fluid test (such as a rapid HIV test) to diagnose HIV.

Using both tests together can help identify individuals co-infected with TB and HIV, allowing for appropriate management and treatment of both conditions.
